Set Work In Progress
Please explain what you have done, why this is needed and how you tested in the commit description. Use your full name in signed off.
Hi @hariharanr@ami.com I have updated the description.
Do management tools really use this?

Yes @gunnar@gmills.xyz, this is expected to be used.
The PrivilegeRegistry endpoint is part of the Redfish model for exposing operation-to-privilege mappings, so adding it improves standards alignment and interoperability.
Done
What tools ? Can you help me understand why this is worth the binary hit here ?

This is not tied to one specific tool.
The intent is to make bmcweb self-contained and standards-complete for
the Redfish PrivilegeRegistry resource.

Why it is worth the binary hit:

It closes a standards gap in registry exposure.
The added data is static registry content (mostly read-only data), not
an always-running background feature.
It is only exercised when the PrivilegeRegistry routes are requested, so
normal request paths are unchanged.
Keeping the mapping in-tree avoids runtime external dependency and keeps
behavior deterministic/offline-safe.
Done
Please wrap the body at 72 chars, not a custom length
I have updated the commit message . Thanks
Done
@gunnar@gmills.xyz @ed@tanous.net Could you please help to review this PR?
Please answer "why?".  Why does a client need to know the required privileges?  Is there an example of a client you can show that usees that info?

I'm not against having this here, but:

1. Please use the files that exist.
2. Please document the use case for this.


As is, this is just exposing the DMTF registry, including lots of things bmcweb doesn't support.  Should we do that, or filter based only on what bmcweb supports (please back up this answer with the spec itself).

Why are you recreating a structure that already exists and is generated?

https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/dd97aa6b21f70700cd3418f5806937372d717324/redfish-core/include/registries/privilege_registry.hpp#L22
please don't use brace construction for nlohmann objects.
